hero.title: Voice-Based Screening for Neurological Disorders
hero.description: A non-invasive technology that analyzes the voice as a signal — designed for early screening, not diagnosis. Parkinson's disease is our first validated application.
hero.note: Screening supports awareness and early conversation — it does not replace a clinical diagnosis.

idea.title: What if your voice could provide a measurable signal?
idea.description: Small variations in voice — pitch, rhythm, timing, stability — can carry information about neurological function. We turn those variations into a structured, quantitative signal.

application.title: Parkinson's Disease
application.description: Parkinson's disease is the first application where our voice-based screening approach has been validated. The technology is designed to flag vocal patterns associated with the condition — supporting earlier awareness and clinical conversation, not replacing a diagnosis.

science.title: Built on Scientific Research
science.description: The technology is being developed through structured scientific and clinical research. Peer-reviewed evidence, validation metrics and clinical collaboration details will be published here as they become available.
science.pillar2Text: Validated in clinical settings — details to be published.
science.pillar3Text: Evidence, methods and limitations will be shared openly.

cta.title: Building the future of neurological screening.
cta.description: We're working with clinicians, researchers and partners to bring voice-based screening into everyday practice.

hero.title: Turning Voice Into a Signal for Neurological Screening
hero.description: Our technology analyzes acoustic and temporal characteristics of the voice using computational methods, identifying patterns that may be relevant to neurological screening. It is designed to support screening — not to provide a diagnosis.

whyVoice.title: Voice carries measurable information
whyVoice.description: Speech and voice contain acoustic and temporal characteristics — such as pitch, rhythm and stability over time — that can be described computationally. These characteristics are the raw material our technology is designed to analyze.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.description: Four steps carry the voice from capture to screening output — each one prepares the signal for the next.

capture.title: Voice Capture
capture.description: The user provides a voice sample through a supported interface.

processing.title: Signal Processing
processing.description: The captured voice is prepared and represented as a signal suitable for analysis.

analysis.title: Computational Analysis
analysis.description: Relevant patterns in the signal are evaluated using our computational models.

screening.title: Screening Output
screening.description: The system produces an output intended to support neurological screening — not a diagnosis.

signalToInsight.title: From signal to insight
signalToInsight.description: A raw recording becomes useful information only after it is represented, characterized and evaluated. The diagram below shows this transformation conceptually — the details of our internal methods are not disclosed.

science.title: Built on Scientific Evidence
science.description: The technology is being developed and evaluated through structured scientific and clinical research. Specific figures, studies and collaborators are not published here yet — they will be added as they become available.

items.researchText: Development follows a research-first methodology grounded in voice and signal analysis.
items.clinicalText: The approach has been evaluated in clinical contexts. Performance metrics will be shared here.
items.collabText: We work with clinical and research partners. Collaborator information will be listed here.
items.validationText: Validation work is ongoing. Outcomes and evidence will be published transparently.

screeningNotice.title: Screening Is Not Diagnosis
screeningNotice.description: This technology is intended to support neurological screening. It does not replace professional medical evaluation, clinical assessment or a definitive diagnosis. A screening result is a signal for further conversation — not a conclusion.

cta.title: Explore the Applications
cta.description: Parkinson's disease is currently the first validated application of our voice-based screening technology.

hero.title: Applications of Voice-Based Neurological Screening
hero.description: The technology is initially focused on Parkinson's disease screening — the first validated application — with potential to support broader neurological research in the future.

current.title: Parkinson's Disease Screening
current.description: Parkinson's disease is the first application of our voice-based technology to have been validated. Voice carries measurable characteristics that may be relevant to neurological assessment. Our system analyzes these voice-derived signals computationally to support screening.
current.note: Screening supports early awareness and clinical conversation. It does not provide a diagnosis.

whyVoice.title: Voice as a measurable signal
whyVoice.description: Speech and voice contain acoustic and temporal characteristics that researchers can study in relation to neurological function. Changes in these characteristics may carry information relevant to screening — which is what our approach is designed to analyze.

workflow.title: A four-step screening pathway
workflow.description: The same underlying approach that powers our Parkinson's screening pathway. The Technology page explains each step in more detail.

future.title: Potential Future Applications
future.description: The underlying approach may have potential for broader neurological research. Applications beyond Parkinson's disease are research directions — not currently validated. We will only present them as applications once the appropriate evidence exists.
future.currentText: The first application of the technology to have been validated for screening support.
future.futureText: The same voice-as-signal approach may support research in other neurological areas. No additional applications are currently validated.
future.footnote: We do not present any future application as a validated capability unless it has been supported by appropriate scientific and clinical evidence.

cta.title: Explore how the technology works

hero.title: The People Behind the Technology
hero.description: Meaningful screening technology is built at the intersection of several disciplines — technology, signal analysis, neuroscience and clinical research. The people behind this project come together from these directions, with a shared focus on scientific rigor.

members.title: A multidisciplinary group
members.description: Profiles of the people behind the technology. Detailed information is being prepared and will be published here.

science.title: Built at the intersection of disciplines
science.description: Developing meaningful screening technology requires more than one kind of expertise. It brings together people working on the technical side of signal and voice analysis with those who understand neurological research and clinical practice. Progress depends on these perspectives being connected — not treated separately.

foundation.title: Grounded in research
foundation.description: Scientific validation is a core part of how the technology is being developed. The Technology page explains the underlying approach and the evidence that supports it.
